title: From Taiwan to California: Teen Swimmer Janet Chen Is Chasing Big Dreams
summary: Imagine racing in a pool with swimmers from all over the world. That’s what Janet Chen did last year at the World Junior Championships! Now this speedy teen from Taiwan is taking an even bigger leap—all the way to California. Janet just announced she’ll swim for Fresno State University starting in fall 2026. “So excited to officially become a Bulldog!” she said. Janet grew up in Hsinchu City and trains with the Taiwanese Swimming Federation. She loves breaststroke and freestyle events. At the 2025 World Juniors, she competed in four races: the 50 and 100 breaststroke, and the 50 and 100 freestyle. But she didn’t stop there. Over the past season, Janet has been on fire, setting personal bests again and again. In October 2025, she swam the 50 freestyle in 26.67 seconds—her fastest ever. Then at the Asian Youth Games, she crushed her 50 breaststroke time with 32.37 seconds. Most recently, at the 2026 National High School Games, she dropped her 100 breaststroke time to 1:13.28 and even tried the 400 IM, finishing in 4:38.24. At Fresno State, Janet’s times would already put her in the ‘C’ final at conference championships, which means she could score points for her team right away. She’ll be joined by other freshmen swimmers and divers, making for a strong squad. It’s a huge move across the Pacific, but Janet sounds ready to make waves. Go Bulldogs!
why_it_matters: Janet's journey shows that with hard work and courage to travel far from home, you can chase your dreams and become part of a team halfway around the world.
